papers.title: The Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic PBC clusters
papers.abstract: We construct and solve the three-colored Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic lattices with periodic boundary conditions. We describe a self-contained procedure which uses finite quotients of orientation- preserving triangle groups to generate regular maps on compact genus-g surfaces. From these, one can extract their lattice connectivity, plaquette structure, homology cycles and Wilson sectors while implementing consistent boundary conditions. On the example of {8, 3} and {12, 3} lattices, we enumerate a selection of quotients with up to 72 vertices, which constitute the discrete steps in a finite-size scaling analysis. For the isotropic point, corresponding to the spin-liquid phase in the thermodynamic limit, we identify the ground state superselection sectors, quantify their deviation from the homogeneous {\pi} flux sector and show how the selected flux background depends on the quotient geometry. We then discuss how the resulting ground state sector degeneracies are entirely generated by physical lattice symmetries acting on both the plaquette fluxes and non-contractible Wilson loops. Finally, we study the behaviour of the finite-size two-vison gap and matter fermion correlations. We find that the gap does not decrease monotonically with increasing system size, while one still recovers the expected algebraic decay of the correlations at the isotropic point, even for the considered modest system sizes.

papers.title: Ultrafast imprinting of fused ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic skyrmions
papers.abstract: Antiferromagnetic skyrmions are promising topologically protected entities for robust storage and THz transport of information. Their generation has so far relied on slow techniques or on specific magnetic structures, which limit their integration into spintronic devices. Here, we demonstrate the imprinting of antiferromagnetic skyrmions within a few picoseconds in a coupled ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic bilayer with a thermal laser pulse. We identify a threshold energy required to initiate the fused skyrmion phase and show that this can be modulated by a magnetic field, enabling deterministic nucleation of antiferromagnetic skyrmions. Compared to conventional slow field-cooling processes to control antiferromagnets we show that laser-induced skyrmion imprinting can be orders of magnitude faster and provides an experimentally feasible route towards ultrafast creation and manipulation of antiferromagnetic skyrmions.

papers.title: Quantum Interband-Coherence-Driven Inverse Faraday Effect in Intrinsic Graphene
papers.abstract: The inverse Faraday effect converts the angular momentum of circularly polarized light into a quasistatic magnetization, providing a fundamental route to ultrafast optical control of magnetic fields. We develop an analytical quantum theory of this effect in intrinsic graphene, where massless Dirac fermions, electron-hole symmetry, and weak spin-orbit coupling suppress conventional population-based interpretations. We show that in intrinsic graphene, the helicity-dependent orbital magnetization arises from the off-diagonal zero-harmonic component of the second-order density matrix, rather than from intraband carrier circulation or diagonal population imbalance. We obtain closed expressions for the induced temporal surface magnetization, its finite-pulse dynamics, and the nonlocal stray magnetic field generated by the two-dimensional (2D) source. Optical helicity, frequency, pulse envelope, and beam profile independently control the response. Our results identify intrinsic graphene as an ideal platform for coherent orbital optomagnetism in 2D Dirac matter.

papers.title: Thermal radiation of nanowires and near-field interaction with substrates: exact computation and proximity approximation
papers.abstract: Radiative heat transfer involving complex nano-objects is difficult to evaluate due to their sub-wavelength size, which induces deviation to macroscopic Planck's opaque surface-to-surface formalism, and due to the small distances involved, which lead to near-field radiative (photon tunneling) effects. As a result, thermal radiation has mostly been neglected in analyses of thermal transport in nanowires. Here, we report on calculations of thermal emission by single nanowires and on the radiative interaction between suspended silicon nanowires and flat substrates. We observe that metallic nanowires can be particularly emissive in comparison to wires made of other materials. While thermal emission from an isolated silicon nanowire is lower than Stefan-Boltzmann's prediction, the radiative exchange with a substrate can be larger by one order of magnitude. The considered configurations also allow benchmarking various levels of common or original approximations, including, in near field, the proximity approximation, the thickness-dependent PA, the electrostatic approach, and the effective emissivity in the far field.

papers.title: Combined magnetic and structural transition state in first-principles calculations
papers.abstract: We present a generalized nudged elastic band (NEB) implementation within potential-based constrained density-functional theory (cDFT) for calculating transition pathways that simultaneously optimize atomic, lattice, and magnetic degrees of freedom. Unlike standard fixed-cell NEB calculations restricted to atomic displacements, our framework consistently couples atomic forces, stresses, and spin torques. The method supports fixed- and variable-cell approaches for collinear and non- collinear magnetic configurations, by incorporating magnetic torques and generalized cell coordinates within the NEB optimization. To validate the methodology, we present benchmark calculations for representative magnetostructural systems. Specifically, we investigate the bcc-to-hcp transformation in Fe and the antiferromagnetic-to-ferromagnetic transition in FeRh using the variable-cell formalism. Furthermore, we examine spin-reversal processes in two-dimensional CrI3 to analyze the influence of spin-orbit coupling on transition paths and their associated energy barriers.

papers.title: Axion electrodynamics and the advection-diffusion structure of TEM modes in hollow-conductor waveguides
papers.abstract: We present a systematic investigation of transverse electromagnetic (TEM) modes in hollow-conductor waveguides filled with a dielectric medium described by axion electrodynamics. While such modes do not propagate in conventional single-conductor waveguides, the coupling of the axion field to an external magnetic field enables their propagation. We show that the resulting TEM modes are governed by an advection-diffusion-type equation for the transverse electrostatic potential, establishing a direct mathematical connection between axion electrodynamics and advection-diffusion phenomena. We illustrate this connection through explicit solutions and field profiles for cylindrical waveguides, considering uniform and rigid rotational drift fields, both individually and in combination, as well as different values of the parameter controlling the advection-to-diffusion ratio (P\'eclet number). These results establish a transport-based framework for understanding how spatial variations of the axion-electrodynamics background shape the transverse electromagnetic fields in hollow-conductor waveguides.

papers.title: Quantitative Theory for the Amplitude of Fluorescence Quantum Beats from Geminate Triplet-Pair Fusion
papers.abstract: We derive the amplitude of fluorescence quantum beats caused by geminate triplet-exciton fusion from the full set of parameters that characterize singlet fission and triplet exciton dynamics. We apply the theory to tetracene and rubrene single crystals. We find that the amplitude depends on the fission time in tetracene, but does not do so in rubrene, where it is determined by the dimensionality of triplet transport. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the experimental data in both materials, for a fission time of the order of 200 ps and isotropic triplet transport in tetracene, and for a triplet hopping time along the herringbone axis of 200-300 ps and anisotropic transport in rubrene.

papers.title: Interference-caged quantum many-body scars: Local ETH-violation witnesses and deformation stability
papers.abstract: Many-body interference can render an exact eigenstate locally nonthermal by canceling a microscopic process active in thermal states. We formulate the Fock-space analogue of compact flat-band localization as \emph{interference caging}: escape amplitudes cancel exactly across the active boundary of a set of product configurations. We give sufficient conditions to reduce this configuration-dependent cancellation to a fixed real-space region, yielding a bounded local caging operator. Its positive square vanishes on the caged eigenstate and witnesses violation of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) if its microcanonical expectation for the same Hamiltonian and energy density remains bounded away from zero in the thermodynamic limit. We call these states \emph{interference-caged quantum many-body scars} (ICQMBS) when they form a vanishing fraction of a symmetry-resolved bulk energy window whose typical eigenstates are locally thermal for every bounded local observable. The mechanism is independent of quasiparticle, algebraic, or symmetry-based constructions and compatible with Hilbert-space fragmentation. Our chiral-shell search constructs exact caged eigenstates from allowed transitions without a preselected wavefunction, target subspace, or ladder operator. We identify local ETH-violation witnesses, test their deformation stability, and demonstrate thermal contrast in two systems. In the spin-1 XY chain, we recover the known scar tower, also describable through quasiparticles and projector embedding, and prove ICQMBS throughout an open interval of compatible exchange couplings in the thermodynamic limit. In the square-lattice quantum dimer model, we construct exact caged eigenstates and local operators from plaquette flips on fixed-width strips under a checkerboard phase deformation; finite-size microcanonical comparisons support thermal contrast.
